title: Knowledge-based_recommender_system
summary:
Knowledge-based recommender systems are a specific type of recommender system that are based on explicit knowledge about the item assortment, user preferences, and recommendation criteria. In complex item domains, customers want to specify their preferences explicitly, and the recommender system must take into account constraints. Neither of these aspects are supported by collaborative filtering and content-based filtering approaches.

Knowledge-based recommender systems are often conversational, meaning user requirements and preferences are elicited within the scope of a feedback loop. A major reason for this is the complexity of the item domain where it is often impossible to articulate all user preferences at once. Furthermore, user preferences are typically not known exactly at the beginning but are constructed within the scope of a recommendation session.

Two main types exist. Search-based (constraint-based) recommenders provide user feedback in terms of answers to questions which restrict the set of relevant items, implemented using constraint search or conjunctive query-based approaches. Navigation-based (case-based) recommenders accept user feedback in terms of critiques which specify change requests regarding the currently recommended item, which are then used for recommendation of the next candidate.

Knowledge-based recommenders exploit semantic user preference knowledge, item knowledge, and recommendation knowledge to identify user-relevant items, which is specifically relevant when dealing with complex and high-involvement items. Both content-based and collaborative systems require significant data about past experiences; in cases where available data is limited, knowledge-based systems can still provide recommendations. Hybrid approaches combining knowledge-based methods with collaborative and content-based filtering can provide more accurate recommendations and help overcome common problems such as cold start, sparsity, and the knowledge engineering bottleneck.
